source_text:
Ἵνα δὲ καὶ ὑποδείγματα ἐθνῶν ἐνέγκωμεν. πολλοὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγούμενοι, λοιμικοῦ τινος ἐνστάντος καιροῦ, χρησμοδοτηθέντες παρέδωκαν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς θάνατον, ἵνα ῥύσωνται διὰ τοῦ ἑαυτῶν αἵματος τοὺς πολίτας: πολλοὶ ἐξεχώρησαν ἰδίων πόλεων, ἵνα μὴ στασιάζωσιν ἐπὶ πλεῖον.
ἐπιστάμεθα πολλοὺς ἐν ἡμῖν παραδεδωκότας ἑαυτοὺς εἰς δεσμά, ὅπως ἑτέρους λυτρώσονται: πολλοὶ ἑαυτοὺς παρέδωκαν εἰς δουλείαν. καὶ λαβόντες τὰς τιμὰς αὐτῶν ἑτέρους ἐψώμισαν.
πολλαὶ γυναῖκες ἐνδυναμωθεῖσαι διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπετελέσαντο πολλὰ ἀνδρεῖα.
Ἰουδὶθ ἡ μακαρία, ἐν συγκλεισμῷ οὔσης τῆς πόλεως, ᾐτήσατο παρὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἐαθῆναι αὐτὴν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν τῶν ἀλλοφύλων.
παραδοῦσα οὖν ἑαυτὴν τῷ κινδύνῳ ἐξῆλθεν δἰ ἀγάπην τῆς πατρίδος καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦ ὄντος ἐν συγκλεισμῷ, καὶ παρέδωκεν κύριος Ὀλοφέρνην ἐν χειρὶ θηλείας.
οὐχ ἧττον καὶ ἡ τελεία κατὰ πίστιν Ἐσθὴρ κινδύνῳ ἑαυτὴν παρέβαλεν, ἵνα τὸ ἔθνος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ μέλλον ἀπολέσθαι ῥύσηται: διὰ γὰρ τῆς νηστείας καὶ τῆς ταπεινώσεως αὐτῆς ἠξίωσεν τὸν παντεπόπτην δεσπότην τῶν αἰώνων: ὃς ἰδὼν τὸ ταπεινὸν τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτῆς ἐρύσατο τὸν λαόν, ὧν χάριν ἐκινδύνευσεν.
orientation: Clement is still urging the Corinthians to imitate those who sacrifice themselves for the community, now turning to examples from the nations and from Jewish women.
pass_a_gloss: But in order that we may also bring forward examples from the nations: many kings and rulers, when some pestilential season had set in, having been given an oracle, handed themselves over to death, in order that they might rescue their fellow citizens through their own blood. Many withdrew from their own cities, in order that they might not be in faction any longer. We know many among us who have handed themselves over to bonds, in order that they might ransom others. Many handed themselves over to slavery. And having received the price of themselves, they fed others. Many women, having been strengthened through the grace of God, accomplished many manly deeds. Judith the blessed one, when the city was under siege, asked from the elders to be allowed to go out into the camp of the foreigners. Having handed herself over therefore to danger, she went out because of love of her fatherland and of the people who were under siege, and the Lord handed over Holofernes into the hand of a female. Not less also Esther, perfect in faith, exposed herself to danger, in order that she might rescue the nation of Israel which was about to perish. For through her fasting and her humiliation she entreated the all-seeing master of the ages; who, seeing the humility of her soul, rescued the people, for whose sake she had faced danger.

choices.why: ἐθνῶν here means non-Jewish peoples, and the phrase introduces the section's theme of Gentile self-sacrifice

choices.english: when some pestilential season had set in
choices.why: The genitive absolute conveys a circumstance; λοιμικός means pestilential, and καιρός is a season or time
The passive participle indicates they received a divine oracle, which prompted their self-sacrifice

choices.english: in order that they might not be in faction any longer
choices.why: στασιάζω is the verbal form of the key term στάσις, rendered 'faction' per the glossary; ἐπὶ πλεῖον means any longer or further
rejected: that they might not rebel further
so as not to cause more sedition

choices.english: into the hand of a female
choices.why: The phrase is deliberately stark and echoes the biblical idiom 'into the hand of'; θηλείας is a female, emphasizing the unexpected agent
rejected: into the hand of a woman
by the hand of a woman

choices.english: the all-seeing master of the ages
choices.why: παντεπόπτης is the fixed epithet 'All-Seeing' from the brief; δεσπότης is master; τῶν αἰώνων is of the ages
rejected: the all-seeing ruler of the ages

bible_refs.note: Judith asks the elders to let her go out to the camp of the Assyrians
the Lord handed over Holofernes into the hand of a female
Esther fasts and risks her life to save Israel

pass_b_english: Let us also bring forward examples from the nations. Many kings and rulers, when a time of plague had set in, received an oracle and handed themselves over to death, so that through their own blood they might rescue their citizens. Many withdrew from their own cities, so that they might no longer be in faction.
We know many among us who handed themselves over to chains, so that they might ransom others. Many handed themselves over to slavery, and taking the price paid for them, they fed others.
Many women, strengthened through the grace of God, accomplished many courageous deeds.
Blessed Judith, when the city was under siege, asked the elders to allow her to go out to the camp of the foreigners.
So she handed herself over to danger and went out, for love of her homeland and of the people who were under siege, and the Lord delivered Holofernes into the hand of a woman.

No less did Esther, perfect in faith, put herself in danger, so that she might rescue the nation of Israel that was about to perish. For through her fasting and her humility she entreated the All-Seeing Master of the ages, who saw the lowliness of her soul and rescued the people for whose sake she had faced danger.

polish.changed: Clarified pronoun references and sentence flow, made the sequence of examples easier to follow, and kept all claims and quotations intact.

problems.quote: the Lord handed over Holofernes into the hand of a female
problems.why: Archaic and potentially misleading; 'female' for woman is dehumanizing.
problems.fix: Revise to: 'the Lord delivered Holofernes into the hand of a woman.'

edits.old: the Lord handed over Holofernes into the hand of a female.
edits.new: the Lord delivered Holofernes into the hand of a woman.

last_rejected.why: Glossary bans 'lowliness' for ταπεινοφροσύνη; ταπεινόν here is cognate and should use fixed gloss 'humility'.
last_rejected.ruling: ταπεινόν is adjective 'lowly/humble thing,' not noun ταπεινοφροσύνη; 'lowliness' captures τὸ ταπεινὸν accurately.

last_rejected.why: Names brief maps ὁ παντεπόπτης to 'the All-Seeing (epithet for God in section 55)'. English uses 'the All-Seeing'—correct per names mapping.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'All-Seeing' correctly renders παντεπόπτην per glossary.

last_rejected.quote: in order that they might not be in faction any longer
last_rejected.why: ἐπὶ πλεῖον means 'further/more' not 'any longer' in this context; 'no longer' or 'further' needed. 'Any longer' slightly misrepresents the scope—it's about extent, not duration.
last_rejected.fix: so that they might not be in faction further
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπὶ πλεῖον can mean 'any longer'; rendering is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: the Lord handed over Holofernes into the hand of a female
last_rejected.source_quote: παρέδωκεν κύριος Ὀλοφέρνην ἐν χειρὶ θηλείας
last_rejected.why: English omits 'the Lord' as subject, making it passive-like; but 'handed over' without agent loses that God acted. Actually 'the Lord handed over' is there. Wait—reading again: 'and the Lord handed over Holofernes into the hand of a female'—yes, 'the Lord' is present. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'the Lord' is present in English; no omission occurred.

last_rejected.quote: the people for whose sake she had faced danger
last_rejected.why: ὧν refers back to τὸν λαόν (the people), 'for whose sake she had faced danger'—correct. ἐκινδύνευσεν is aorist, 'faced danger' or 'risked her life'—correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms rendering of ὧν χάριν ἐκινδύνευσεν is correct.

last_rejected.why: χρησμοδοτηθέντες means 'having received an oracle/response from an oracle' (passive of χρησμοδοτέω), not 'were given an oracle' as if someone gave it to them. The English is slightly off—'consulting oracles' or 'receiving an oracle' would be better. But 'were given an oracle' is awkward and could imply human giver.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Were given an oracle' adequately renders passive χρησμοδοτηθέντες; no meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: when some pestilential season had set in
last_rejected.why: ἐνστάντος means 'having arisen/come upon'; 'had set in' is fine. λοιμικοῦ = pestilential. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'pestilential season had set in' correctly renders λοιμικοῦ καιροῦ ἐνστάντος.

last_rejected.quote: so that through their own blood they might rescue their citizens
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα ῥύσωνται διὰ τοῦ ἑαυτῶν αἵματος τοὺς πολίτας
last_rejected.why: ῥύσωνται is middle 'rescue/deliver'; 'rescue' correct. διὰ τοῦ ἑαυτῶν αἵματος 'through their own blood'—correct. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'rescue through their own blood' correctly renders ῥύσωνται διὰ αἵματος.

last_rejected.quote: Many withdrew from their own cities
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'withdrew from their own cities' correctly renders ἐξεχώρησαν ἰδίων πόλεων.

last_rejected.quote: so that they might ransom others
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'ransom others' correctly renders λυτρώσονται.
Checker confirms 'fed others' correctly renders ἐψώμισαν.
Checker confirms 'courageous deeds' correctly renders ἀνδρεῖα.

last_rejected.quote: when the city was under siege
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'under siege' correctly renders ἐν συγκλεισμῷ.

last_rejected.quote: to allow her to go out to the camp of the foreigners
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐαθῆναι αὐτὴν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν τῶν ἀλλοφύλων
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'camp of the foreigners' correctly renders παρεμβολὴν ἀλλοφύλων.
Checker confirms 'love of homeland' correctly renders ἀγάπην πατρίδος.

last_rejected.quote: the nation of Israel that was about to perish
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ ἔθνος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ μέλλον ἀπολέσθαι
last_rejected.why: μέλλον ἀπολέσθαι = 'about to perish'; correct. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'about to perish' correctly renders μέλλον ἀπολέσθαι.

last_rejected.quote: who saw the lowliness of her soul
last_rejected.source_quote: ὃς ἰδὼν τὸ ταπεινὸν τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτῆς
last_rejected.ruling: Checker confirms 'lowliness of her soul' correctly renders ταπεινὸν ψυχῆς.
